description: Congresswoman Terri Sewell (AL-07) seeks a creative Digital and Press Fellow to help her legislative and communications teams execute the office's press, outreach, and social media strategy. A major portion of the office's legislative work is centered on voting rights, healthcare, and economic equity. The office also has a robust district outreach agenda, which includes both virtual and in-person programming throughout the year. As a member of the press team, the Digital and Press Fellow will be engaged in all of this work. This position is paid and a commitment of three months is expected.
responsibilities: Drafting social media and outreach content with an emphasis on videos and graphic design
Various other tasks to support the office's press, outreach, and social media strategy
qualifications: Creative self-starter with a high level of attention to detail
Willingness to work collaboratively to advance the office's goals
Strong writing, video editing, graphic design, and digital communication skills
Prior experience creating social media and digital content is preferred
Past experience in communications and experience with Adobe suite, Canva, Streamyard, Zoom, and other digital and virtual platforms is preferred
how_to_apply: Email a resume, two writing samples (700 word max), and samples of original digital content (graphics, videos, etc.) to AL07.DigitalFellow@mail.house.gov with "First and Last Name, Digital & Press Fellow" in the subject line by Friday, May 24th.
equal_opportunity: The office is an equal opportunity employer and doesn't discriminate on the basis of race, sex, color, age, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, or disability.

position_title: Health Policy Law Clerk Or Graduate Student Research Intern
description: The Democratic Staff of the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs seeks a law clerk or graduate student research intern to focus on health policy and legislative issues for the Summer 2024 semester. The law clerk or intern will work primarily with Health Subcommittee staff on research projects related to the implementation of previously passed legislation, assisting with the development of new legislative proposals, and assisting with other veterans' healthcare-related oversight efforts. This position will be well-suited to individuals with interests in veterans' issues, healthcare policy, and women's health. This paid, full-time or part-time, in-person position is based in Washington, D.C.
responsibilities: Drafting memos, letters, and other written materials
Attending briefings and hearings for staff
Working with Health Subcommittee staff on research projects related to the implementation of previously passed legislation
Assisting with the development of new legislative proposals
Assisting with other veterans' healthcare-related oversight efforts
qualifications: Second- or third-year law students or graduate students with a demonstrated interest in public service
Ability to pay close attention to detail
Excellent research, writing, and analytical skills
Ability to excel in fast-paced environments
how_to_apply: Please complete the online application at https://democratsveterans.house.gov/opportunities. The deadline to apply is May 17, 2024.
